title: S&P 500 & Dow Slip Into Correction as Nasdaq Erases 2026 Gains, Anthropic Triggers AI Sell‑off
body:
The U.S. equity market entered correction territory on Friday as the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped below their recent peaks, while the Nasdaq Composite erased the gains it had logged earlier this year. The catalyst was a sharp drop in the stock of Anthropic, the artificial‑intelligence startup that debuted on the public markets just a day earlier, prompting investors to cash in on the broader AI‑driven rally rather than extend it.

Anthropic opened at a lofty valuation after its IPO, but the stock quickly lost momentum, falling more than 12% from its debut price by the close of trading. The sell‑off reverberated across technology‑heavy indices, dragging the Nasdaq down 1.8% and pulling the broader market into correction mode—a decline of at least 10% from recent highs. The S&P 500 finished the session down 1.4%, and the Dow slipped 1.2%, marking the worst day for the major averages in the past week.

Analysts attribute the pullback to a combination of profit‑taking and a reassessment of the sustainability of the AI hype that has buoyed markets since the start of the year. “The Anthropic IPO was the final piece of a very aggressive AI narrative,” said Laura Chen, senior equity strategist at Meridian Capital. “When the stock stumbled, it forced investors to confront the fact that much of the rally was built on expectations rather than earnings.” The correction follows a volatile stretch that saw the Nasdaq climb more than 30% year‑to‑date on the back of strong earnings from cloud providers and semiconductor firms, but also experienced intermittent setbacks as regulators signaled tighter scrutiny of AI applications.

The broader market reaction also highlighted the fragility of the “AI premium” that many high‑growth companies have been enjoying. Shares of Nvidia, Microsoft, and Alphabet—all of which have positioned AI as a core growth engine—experienced modest declines of 2% to 3% as investors rotated out of speculative bets into more defensive sectors. Meanwhile, traditional safe‑haven assets such as Treasury bonds and gold saw modest inflows, suggesting a shift toward risk‑averse positioning amid the uncertainty.

From a macroeconomic perspective, the correction arrives at a time when the Federal Reserve remains hawkish, with interest rates held at a 23‑year high and no clear indication of imminent easing. Higher borrowing costs have already pressured rate‑sensitive sectors like real estate and consumer discretionary, and the added volatility in tech stocks could compound the headwinds. “We’re seeing a confluence of factors—tight monetary policy, lingering supply‑chain concerns, and now a reality check on AI valuations—that could keep the market choppy for the next few weeks,” noted Mark Alvarez, chief economist at Global Insights.

Looking ahead, market participants will be watching the upcoming earnings season for clues on whether AI‑related revenue streams can translate into sustainable profitability. Companies that can demonstrate concrete AI integration into their core products, rather than merely capitalizing on buzz, may be better positioned to weather the correction. In the meantime, investors are likely to adopt a more cautious stance, favoring quality stocks with solid balance sheets and clear cash‑flow generation. The next major catalyst could be the Federal Reserve’s policy meeting later this month, which may either reinforce the current defensive tilt or provide the impetus for a renewed risk‑on rally if signals of a policy pause emerge.
